text:
Maria V: quick question — can we align on how the API should behave during a canary rollforward where model pins and response shapes diverge? saw two weirds in staging this morning: client got 200 + extra fields (schema v1 plus new v2 keys) and another client got 404 model-not-found while the pinned variant was being garbage-collected. cc @Jon P @Kevin L

Jon P: For the GC 404 case — that's a bug. pinned model should never be collected while a customer has an active pin. filing a follow-up. For the response-shape case, we want a strict contract guarantee unless the client opts into negotiation.

Jon P: TL;DR: default = strict contract (no unknown fields), opt-in header = permissive/merge fallback. Suggested headers: `X-Model-Version: 2026-03-09` and `Accept-Contract: v1` (or `Accept-Contract: merge-v1-v2`).

Kevin L: re: headers — what should the SDK do by default? keep old behavior (merge) or error out? most customers expect non-breaking, but internal infra prefers fail-fast for regressions.

Sara T: Agree. Suggest SDK default = strict (fail on unknown fields) for server-side libs, but a client flag `allow_contract_overlap=true` for user-level libs. We'll surface this in the changelog + migration guide.

Oliver M: Also call out runtime fallback ordering. my proposal: 1) exact version match 2) compatible variant (quantized/fast) 3) fallback to host-model with compatibility header 4) return 409 or 412 when nothing matches. That keeps behavior deterministic.

Jon P: +1 to ordered fallback. Also: prefer 412 (Precondition Failed) with a structured error payload so SDKs can decide auto-upgrade vs. user-visible error. Example error body: ```json
{"error":"contract_mismatch","expected":"v1","observed":"v2","resolution":"provide Accept-Contract header or pin to v2"}```

Maria V: deploy-bot, any canary timeline notes? we want to coordinate docs and dedicated customers.

deploy-bot: Canary for runtime v2 scheduled: 2026-03-17 02:00 UTC -> 2026-03-17 06:00 UTC. Will target 10% traffic initially. Notifications will post to #incidents if SLA signals.

Kevin L: For pinned-model GC fix, I'll open a PR to the controller to mark pinned artifacts as protected until release-window passes. also will add a metric `pin_protection_hits`.

Sara T: I'll draft the deprecation/migration timeline: - notify customers 30d before forced unpin removal - provide opt-in `compatibility_mode` for 90d - full enforcement after 120d. Share draft in docs repo by EOD tomorrow.

Jon P: One more implementation detail: add `X-Contract-Warning` header when we return 200 with extra fields (for permissive mode) so telemetry can track regressions.

Oliver M: SDK change: bump major for server-side libs and add a runtime flag `REDWOOD_ALLOW_CONTRACT_MERGE`. client libs get minor with default strict. I'll include migration examples.

Maria V: thanks all — action items: @Kevin L fix GC + metric, @Oliver M SDK PR, @Sara T draft timeline + docs, @Jon P update error payload schema and header names. I'll update the API spec and post a short changelog entry before the canary window.

Jon P: ping when the spec is updated and I'll run compatibility tests against the canary.

Maria V: will do. :thumbsup:
